unit.title: Transformations
unit.blurb: Reading and plotting coordinates in all four quadrants, translating, reflecting in horizontal, vertical and diagonal lines, and rotating shapes by 90° about a vertex.
unit.subject: maths

O1.t: Read and plot coordinates in all four quadrants, and translate shapes.

O2.t: Reflect 2D shapes in horizontal, vertical and diagonal mirror lines.

O3.t: Rotate shapes 90° about a vertex, clockwise or anticlockwise.

p: A point is written **(x, y)**: go **across** first, then **up or down**. (−3, 2) is 3 left and 2 up.
The axes cross at the **origin** (0, 0). Negative x is left; negative y is down.
A **translation** slides a shape without turning it. 'Move 3 right and 2 down' adds 3 to x and takes 2 from y.
(2, 5) and (5, 2) are different points: x always comes first.

p: When a shape is **reflected**, each point ends up the **same distance** from the mirror line on the other side.
Reflect in the **y-axis**: (x, y) → (−x, y). Reflect in the **x-axis**: (x, y) → (x, −y). Reflect in **y = x**: (x, y) → (y, x).
A point 2 squares from the mirror line must end up 2 squares from it on the other side.

p: A **rotation** turns a shape about a fixed point called the **centre of rotation**. Give the **angle** (90°, 180°) and the **direction** (clockwise or anticlockwise).
Rotating 90° clockwise about the origin: (x, y) → (y, −x). A half turn (180°): (x, y) → (−x, −y).
Trace the shape, hold the centre with a pencil, and turn the paper.
